source.title: Understanding deep learning (still) requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

record.file_problem: The full text is present. The supplied text includes the article and appendices; some table formatting is flattened.
record.tranche_reason: This is the original study: it directly trains standard neural-network architectures on randomized labels and inputs and reports training and test performance.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for true labels, corrupted labels, random labels, shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs. It also reports regularizer ablations. Cited results from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The supplied text is arXiv:1611.03530v2, an original source for V1–V5. It directly measures random-label fitting, convergence time, unstructured-input fitting, corruption-dependent generalization, and regularizer ablations. The different study identifier does not make these independent replication results.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that several successful architectures have enough effective capacity to memorize arbitrary training labels, that optimization remains empirically easy despite failed generalization, and that traditional complexity measures and explicit regularization do not adequately explain generalization. Their broad summary should retain the reported exceptions: incomplete ImageNet fitting, Alexnet's failure with weight decay, and modified training settings for augmentation experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies the original randomized-label and input experiments, including true-label comparisons, to standard CIFAR10 and ImageNet architectures; it is itself an original source for V1–V5.
record.method_sensitivity: CIFAR10 Alexnet with weight decay fails to converge on random labels while the other reported CIFAR10 models fit; ImageNet random-label top-1 accuracy remains below perfect; convergence slows as label corruption increases; regularization and data augmentation change fitting and true-label test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 constructs a two-layer ReLU network with 2n+d weights that represents arbitrary labels on n distinct samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide ReLU networks have universal finite-sample expressivity; this construction does not establish fitting by stochastic gradient training.

record.problems: Exact intermediate values for convergence slowdown and corruption-dependent test error are presented only in figures. Table 1 formatting is flattened, making some model-to-value assignments uncertain. ImageNet random-label fitting is not perfect under the reported unchanged settings.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were omitted. Rows R22–R25 use only the no-augmentation/no-weight-decay test-accuracy entries; some Table 1 associations are uncertain because the supplied table is flattened.

untested.parts: No measurement separates learning shared real-data patterns from subsequent memorization of noisy labels. Comparing convergence curves on separate true-label and random-label datasets does not establish that order.
The independent contribution of dropout is not isolated: the ImageNet random-label table has no dropout-only condition.

missing.what: ImageNet true-label regularizer removal: Inception V3 achieves 59.80% top-1 test accuracy without augmentation, dropout or weight decay, versus 77.84% with all three. With augmentation alone it achieves 72.95%. These quantify the generalization benefit and the retained performance without explicit regularization.
Inception without batch normalization fits CIFAR10 random labels with 100% training accuracy and 10.12% test accuracy, with random cropping and weight decay off.
missing.locator: Table 1, Inception w/o BatchNorm random-label condition

missing.what: The ImageNet weight-decay-only random-label condition has 0.12% top-1 test accuracy, near the 0.1% chance baseline; its 87.81% training accuracy is already recorded in R7.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are issued because the supplied text is the listed original source for V1–V5. Original-source status follows the supplied title and arXiv identifier, despite the record's DOI. V6 is not tested. Exact intermediate figure values remain unavailable, but explicit prose supports the qualitative V2 and V4 outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: Tests several standard image-classification architectures on CIFAR10 and ImageNet; the ImageNet model does not reach perfect training accuracy without hyperparameter tuning.
Reports a relative convergence-time curve, but no exact slowdown values in the text.
Tests shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs on CIFAR10; no ImageNet unstructured-input experiment is reported.
Tests varying label corruption on CIFAR10 and reports perfect training fit and rising test error; exact intermediate values are shown only in a figure.
Tests weight decay and data augmentation on CIFAR10 and explicit regularizers on ImageNet; dropout is tested for ImageNet, not as a separate CIFAR10 ablation.
The study does not test the training order of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noise.

statements.correction: Supplied source: arXiv:1611.03530v2, dated 26 February 2017. Section 2.1: CIFAR10 Inception learning curves for shared permutations, independent per-image permutations and Gaussian inputs. Section 1.1: zero training error with random-noise inputs.
statements.problem: The input-randomization results are supported, but the supplied text is the 2017 original preprint and cannot verify their appearance in the 2021 account or its reviewed-publication status.

statements.correction: Table 4: weight-decay training accuracy, Inception 100%, MLP 3x512 100%, MLP 1x512 99.21%; cropping 99.93%; flipping and rotation 99.28%. Table 1: true-label test accuracy, Inception 89.05% with cropping and weight decay versus 85.75% without both; Alexnet 81.22% versus 76.07%. Appendix E already specifies online minibatch accuracy.
